facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A day on Venus is longer than its year. Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: There is no sound in space. Sound needs a medium, like air, to travel through, and space is a near-vacuum.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: The human body constantly emits infrared light, meaning people glow faintly, just not in a range our eyes can detect.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A bolt of lightning is roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Water expands when it freezes, instead of contracting like most substances. This is why ice floats.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Diamond and graphite, the material in pencil lead, are made of the exact same element, carbon, just arranged differently.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Helium is the only element that was discovered in space before it was found on Earth.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Table salt is made of two elements, sodium and chlorine, that are both dangerous on their own.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Gold is so unreactive that it doesn't tarnish or rust, which is part of why it has been valuable for thousands of years.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: The stomach lining replaces itself every few days because stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve it.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Humans share about 60% of their DNA with bananas.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: The human brain uses about 20% of the body's total energy, despite being only about 2% of body weight.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Bones are about five times stronger than steel of the same weight.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: The human heart beats around 100,000 times a day without any conscious effort.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: Mount Everest grows about 4mm taller every year due to tectonic plate movement.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: The Sahara Desert was a lush, green landscape with lakes and rivers around 10,000 years ago.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: There is enough water in Earth's atmosphere at any moment to cover the planet in about 1 inch of rain if it all fell at once.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: Lightning strikes the Earth about 100 times every second.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: A single teaspoon of soil can contain billions of microorganisms.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: Zero was not always considered a number. Many ancient civilizations had no symbol or concept for it.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Honeybees build their hives using hexagons because that shape uses the least wax while storing the most honey, an efficient geometric solution.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A feather and a hammer dropped together in a vacuum, with no air resistance, hit the ground at exactly the same time.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Glass is not a true crystalline solid; it is an amorphous solid, meaning its atoms are arranged more like a liquid that has been frozen in place.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Sound travels about four times faster through water than it does through air.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Earth's magnetic poles have flipped many times over its history, with north and south swapping places.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe, far more than oxygen, which is only about 21%.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water, a chemical process called oxidation.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Pure water has a neutral pH of 7, exactly in the middle of the acid-base scale, which runs from 0 to 14.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Only two elements on the periodic table are liquid at room temperature: mercury and bromine.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: An adult human body is made up of an estimated 37 trillion cells.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Plants release oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, which is why forests are often called the lungs of the planet.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: The human body contains enough iron to make a small nail, though it is spread across the blood and tissues rather than concentrated in one place.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Identical twins do not have completely identical fingerprints, even though they share the same DNA.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, due to the copper-based protein it uses to carry oxygen.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Bacteria outnumber human cells in the human body, with trillions of microbes living mostly in the gut.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored or mapped in detail.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: There are more active volcanoes underwater than there are on land.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: Earth's atmosphere has no clear edge; it gradually thins out into space over hundreds of kilometres.

facts.subject: Astronomy
facts.fact: Jupiter is so massive that it could fit all the other planets in the solar system inside it combined.

facts.subject: Astronomy
facts.fact: Most of the stars visible in the night sky are actually much brighter than the Sun, but they appear dimmer because they are far away.

facts.subject: Astronomy
facts.fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimetres per year.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: A circle has infinite lines of symmetry, more than any other basic shape.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: Prime numbers become rarer as numbers get larger, but mathematicians have proven there are infinitely many of them.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure in the world for over 3,800 years.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: Ancient Egyptians used a 365-day calendar thousands of years before the modern calendar was developed.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: World War One ended in 1918, but the official peace treaty, the Treaty of Versailles, was not signed until 1919.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The ancient Mali Empire, under Mansa Musa, was once considered one of the wealthiest civilizations in recorded history.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Benin Bronzes, created by skilled artisans in the Kingdom of Benin, are some of the most celebrated metal artworks in African history.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: It took explorers over 400 years after Columbus's voyages to fully map the coastlines of the Americas.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The printing press, invented in the 1400s, made books dramatically cheaper and helped literacy spread across Europe.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Great Wall of China was not built all at once; it was constructed and extended by multiple dynasties over more than 2,000 years.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: The Nile is often cited as the longest river in the world, stretching over 6,600 kilometres through northeastern Africa.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, but Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller when measured from base to peak.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country in the world.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Africa is the only continent that lies across all four hemispheres: north, south, east, and west.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Antarctica is technically the largest desert in the world, since deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Lagos is one of the fastest-growing cities in the world, with its population having grown dramatically over the past few decades.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: The Pacific Ocean is so large it covers more area than all of Earth's continents combined.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: The equator passes through 13 countries, including several in Africa such as Kenya, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: The word "set" has more distinct meanings in the dictionary than almost any other word in the English language.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: English borrows words from over 350 other languages, which is part of why its spelling rules have so many exceptions.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: William Shakespeare is credited with inventing or popularizing over 1,700 words still used in English today.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: "I am" is the shortest complete sentence in the English language, since it has both a subject and a verb.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: The longest word in widely used English dictionaries without repeating any letter is "uncopyrightable," at 15 letters.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: The question mark and exclamation mark did not exist in early written English; punctuation systems developed gradually over centuries.

facts.subject: Civic Education
facts.fact: A democracy is a system of government where citizens choose their leaders through voting, rather than power being inherited or seized.

facts.subject: Civic Education
facts.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted in 1948, was one of the first global agreements outlining basic rights for all people.

facts.subject: Economics
facts.fact: Barter, trading goods directly without money, was the main system of exchange before currency was widely adopted.

facts.subject: Economics
facts.fact: The first known paper money was used in China over a thousand years ago, long before it appeared in Europe.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: A haiku is a traditional Japanese poetic form made up of just three lines and 17 syllables in total.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart, published in 1958, has been translated into more than 50 languages.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: Ancient Greek plays were performed in massive outdoor theatres that could hold tens of thousands of spectators at once.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: A palindrome is a word or phrase that reads the same forwards and backwards, like "level" or "madam."

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: The novel Don Quixote, published in the early 1600s, is often considered one of the first modern novels ever written.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: Wole Soyinka became the first African writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986.

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: A federal system of government divides power between a central government and smaller regional or state governments.

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: Most modern governments divide power into three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial, to prevent any single branch from having too much control.

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: Universal suffrage, the right of all adult citizens to vote regardless of gender or property ownership, only became common worldwide in the 20th century.

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: A constitution is a country's foundational legal document, outlining how its government is structured and what powers it holds.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Topsoil, the most fertile layer of soil, can take hundreds of years to form naturally but can be eroded away in just a few seasons of poor farming practice.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Crop rotation, growing different crops in the same field across seasons, helps maintain soil fertility and reduce pest buildup.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: A cow has four stomach compartments, which allow it to digest tough plant material like grass that humans cannot break down.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Nitrogen-fixing plants like beans and groundnuts can pull nitrogen from the air and add it back into the soil, naturally improving fertility.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Irrigation systems have been used by farmers for thousands of years, with some of the earliest known systems dating back to ancient Mesopotamia.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A rainbow forms when light is refracted, reflected, and dispersed inside water droplets, splitting white light into its different colours.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: An object in motion stays in motion unless acted on by an external force, a principle known as Newton's First Law, or the law of inertia.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another, a principle known as the law of conservation of energy.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A circuit must form a complete loop for electric current to flow; breaking the loop anywhere stops the current entirely.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: An atom is mostly empty space; if the nucleus were the size of a marble, the electrons would orbit roughly a kilometre away.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: A solution is a type of mixture where one substance dissolves completely into another, like sugar dissolving in water.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Exothermic reactions release heat into their surroundings, while endothermic reactions absorb heat from their surroundings.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Humans breathe out roughly the same volume of air they breathe in, but with less oxygen and more carbon dioxide.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: A food chain shows energy moving from one organism to another, starting with producers like plants and moving through different levels of consumers.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Some plants can reproduce both sexually, through seeds, and asexually, through runners or cuttings.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: The human skeleton is constantly remodelling itself, with old bone tissue being broken down and replaced with new tissue over time.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: Rocks are classified into three main types: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic, based on how they form.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: The water cycle has no real starting point; water continuously moves between the ocean, atmosphere, and land through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

facts.subject: Astronomy
facts.fact: It takes Earth about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun, which is why an extra day is added every four years in a leap year.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: The term "algebra" comes from the Arabic word al-jabr, meaning "reunion of broken parts," from a 9th-century mathematics text.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Berlin Conference of 1884 to 1885 saw European powers divide up African territory without consulting any African leaders.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule on October 1, 1960.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Roman Empire at its peak controlled territory across three continents: Europe, Africa, and Asia.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Nigeria is one of the largest producers of crude oil in Africa, with reserves concentrated mainly in the Niger Delta region.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Contour lines on a map connect points of equal elevation, and lines drawn close together indicate steep terrain.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions, while climate describes long-term average weather patterns over years or decades.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: English has eight traditional parts of speech: nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, and interjections.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: Skimming and scanning are two different reading strategies; skimming gets a general overview, while scanning searches for specific information.

facts.subject: Civic Education
facts.fact: Citizenship can usually be acquired in three ways: by birth, by descent from a parent, or by naturalization after meeting legal requirements.

facts.subject: Economics
facts.fact: Scarcity, the basic economic problem, exists because human wants are unlimited but resources to satisfy them are limited.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: A metaphor directly states that one thing is another, while a simile compares two things using "like" or "as."

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: The United Nations was founded in 1945 after the Second World War, aiming to prevent future global conflicts through diplomacy.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Integrated pest management combines biological, chemical, and physical methods to control pests while minimizing environmental harm.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: All data in a computer, including text, images, and sound, is ultimately stored and processed as combinations of just two digits: 0 and 1.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: The first computer virus to spread over a network, called the Morris Worm, was created in 1988 and accidentally caused major disruption.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: A byte is made up of 8 bits, and a single bit can only hold a value of 0 or 1.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: The first computer programmer is widely considered to be Ada Lovelace, who wrote algorithms for a mechanical computer in the 1840s.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: A balanced diet should include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water, since each plays a different role in the body.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize and fight specific diseases before a person is ever exposed to the real infection.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: Washing hands properly with soap for at least 20 seconds removes far more germs than rinsing with water alone.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: The recovery position is used to keep an unconscious but breathing person safe by preventing them from choking on fluids.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Metals feel colder than wood at the same temperature because metal conducts heat away from your skin much faster.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Radio waves, light, and X-rays are all part of the same electromagnetic spectrum, differing only in wavelength and energy.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: A concave lens spreads light rays apart, while a convex lens brings them together to a focal point.

facts.subject: Physics
facts.fact: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, which is part of why it is harder to breathe at the top of tall mountains.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Ionic bonds form when electrons are transferred between atoms, while covalent bonds form when electrons are shared.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points by heating a mixture and collecting the vapour as it cools back into liquid.

facts.subject: Chemistry
facts.fact: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust, even though it was only isolated by scientists in the 1800s.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Living things are organized into a hierarchy of groups, from kingdom down to species, based on shared characteristics.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Nerve impulses can travel through the human body at speeds of over 100 metres per second.

facts.subject: Biology
facts.fact: Digestion begins in the mouth, where the enzyme amylase in saliva starts breaking down starches before food even reaches the stomach.

facts.subject: Earth Science
facts.fact: Earth's continents were once joined together in a single landmass called Pangaea, before slowly drifting apart over millions of years.

facts.subject: Astronomy
facts.fact: The Milky Way galaxy contains an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars, and our Sun is just one of them.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: The mean, median, and mode are three different ways of describing the "average" or central value in a set of data.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: The angles in any triangle always add up to exactly 180 degrees, regardless of the triangle's shape or size.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: The Trans-Saharan trade routes connected West Africa to North Africa and the Mediterranean for centuries, exchanging gold, salt, and other goods.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: Britain formally abolished the slave trade in 1807, though slavery itself continued in some British territories for decades afterward.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: Ancient Mesopotamia, located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is often called the cradle of civilization.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: A plateau is a flat, elevated area of land, distinguishing it from a plain, which is flat but at a lower elevation.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Urbanization describes the movement of people from rural areas into cities, a trend that has accelerated rapidly across Africa in recent decades.

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: Personification gives human qualities to non-human things, like saying "the wind whispered through the trees."

facts.subject: English Language
facts.fact: English has 12 main verb tenses, formed by combining past, present, and future with simple, continuous, perfect, and perfect continuous aspects.

facts.subject: Civic Education
facts.fact: The rule of law means that everyone, including leaders, is subject to and accountable under the law, not above it.

facts.subject: Economics
facts.fact: When demand for a product rises while supply stays the same, prices typically increase, according to basic economic theory.

facts.subject: Literature
facts.fact: A sonnet is a 14-line poem, often written in iambic pentameter, with a structured rhyme scheme.

facts.subject: Government
facts.fact: Local governments typically handle community-level matters like waste collection, local roads, and primary education, while national governments handle broader policy.

facts.subject: Agricultural Science
facts.fact: Poultry farming is one of the fastest ways to produce animal protein, since chickens grow to market size much faster than cattle or goats.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: A URL, or web address, is essentially a human-readable way of pointing to a numerical IP address that identifies a specific server.

facts.subject: Computer Science
facts.fact: Open-source software allows anyone to view, modify, and distribute its source code, unlike proprietary software which keeps its code private.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: Regular physical exercise has been shown to reduce symptoms of stress and anxiety, partly by triggering the release of mood-boosting chemicals in the brain.

facts.subject: Health Education
facts.fact: Vitamin C deficiency causes a disease called scurvy, which was historically common among sailors on long voyages without fresh fruit.

facts.subject: Financial Literacy
facts.fact: Compound interest means earning interest not just on the money you saved, but also on the interest that money has already earned.

facts.subject: Financial Literacy
facts.fact: A budget tracks income against expenses, helping identify whether someone is spending more than they earn.

facts.subject: Financial Literacy
facts.fact: A credit score is a number that represents how reliably a person has repaid borrowed money in the past, which lenders use to assess risk.

facts.subject: Creative Arts
facts.fact: Primary colours, red, blue, and yellow, cannot be created by mixing other colours, but can be combined to create every other colour.

facts.subject: Creative Arts
facts.fact: A musical octave contains 12 distinct notes, including both the natural notes and the sharps or flats between them.

facts.subject: Creative Arts
facts.fact: Adire is a traditional Yoruba textile art form from Nigeria, made using resist-dyeing techniques to create intricate patterns on cloth.

facts.subject: Physical Education
facts.fact: Aerobic exercise strengthens the heart and lungs over time, while anaerobic exercise like sprinting builds short-burst muscle power.

facts.subject: Physical Education
facts.fact: A standard football match consists of two 45-minute halves, plus any added stoppage time for delays during play.
